svg.title: Zero travel time preserves a forcing boundary
svg.desc: Exact fixed-input slice s equals minus three halves, z equals w, transverse covector zeta nonzero, for F equals g(t) h(s) delta(z-w), g positive on zero to one with support zero to one. The forcing wavefront times are the closed interval zero to one. The correction i h(s) integral from s to t of g has wavefront times zero to infinity. Strict forward composition has times strictly greater than zero and excludes the required source boundary. Time positions use x equals 410 plus 160t. Filled circles mean included points; an empty circle means excluded. Right arrows indicate continuation to infinity. Proof: directional transport lesson, Exercise 1, DT10 to DT12. Original vector source, CC0.

g.text: A source boundary belongs to its forward correction
Fixed input: s = −3/2, z = w, ζ ≠ 0; the time flow is ∂t.
At t = 0, g and all its derivatives vanish; its wavefront support still includes the boundary.
Use (Δ* ∪ C⁺) ◦ WF′(F) to retain zero travel time. Exercise 1 proves the exact kernel statement.
